Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Audit logging capabilities (what we covered)
- Admin activity logs: who changed roles/permissions, console actions, and RBAC changes.
- API logs: request/response metrics, request IDs, timestamps, and requestor identity.
- Exportability: logs can be exported to S3 / GCS / Azure Blob or downloaded as JSON/CSV.
- Immutability: write-once retention options via WORM storage for audit-grade retention plus tamper-evident checksums.

2) Compliance status
- SOC 2: we maintain controls across security and availability; we have a SOC 2 Type II engagement in flight and expect a report in Q1 2027.
- GDPR/HIPAA: we support contractual controls and data processing addenda; HIPAA customers can use Private deployments and customer-managed KMS.

3) Ask / next steps
- Sam: you mentioned a vendor security questionnaire — please attach it here and we’ll start filling it out.
- We’ll send a short SOC 2 summary and an audit-logging overview doc for your security team.
- If helpful, propose a 30-minute follow-up with our security/infra lead next week to walk through logs and export flows.

Attachments: redwood-audit-logging-overview.pdf, redwood-soc2-status-20261120.pdf

Hi all — copying answers inline for Section A and a short log summary. Happy to hop on the follow-up call next week.

SOC 2 status:
- Current state: We have a SOC 2 Type II engagement underway. Control implementation is complete across common criteria (access control, system operations, change management).
- Expected: Final Type II report targeted for end of Q1 2027 (we expect to have an interim attestation and control description available earlier).
- What we can share now: control matrix, security policy docs, and a redacted SOC 2 control description PDF (attached: redwood-soc2-status-20261120.pdf).

Audit logging specifics:
- Admin activity logs: capture user identity, action, resource, IP, timestamp, and request ID. Events include role changes, permission grants/revokes, user creation/deletion, and console-based config changes.
- API logs: capture full request metadata (requestor id, endpoint, params), response codes, latency, token usage, and request IDs. We correlate request IDs with trace IDs for sampling/traceability.
- Exportability: logs can be exported on-demand or streamed. Supported sinks: S3 (presigned or push-to-customer-bucket), GCS, Azure Blob, and syslog/webhook integrations. Exports available as JSON or CSV.
- Immutability & retention: immutability is provided via write-once retention policies (WORM) when enabled on export sinks; within Redwood we maintain tamper-evident checksums and append-only storage for audit trails. Retention windows are configurable per-account; defaults are 90 days for API logs and 365 days for admin logs, with options up to 7 years for enterprise concierge customers.

Sample (redacted) JSON snippet for an API log export:
{
  "timestamp": "2026-11-19T22:34:12Z",
  "request_id": "req_9b8f7a6c",
  "user_id": "user_1234",
  "endpoint": "/v1/generate",
  "status_code": 200,
  "latency_ms": 123
}

Next steps we propose:
- We'll populate Section A of your questionnaire and return within the day.
- Share the SOC 2 summary and a link to the redacted controls doc (Drive link included).
- Schedule a 30-minute technical review next week (please propose 2 slots).

Attachments included: redwood-audit-logging-overview.pdf, redwood-soc2-status-20261120.pdf
